ask.summary: Should 3+ questions name two options in the question text (either/or) or stay open, given the must MOD-03-U02 says the card has no answer choices?
ask.context:
All 50 questions in the 3+ deck now pass the one-answer rule; CI is green and both reviewers accept the content. 46 of them get there by naming two options in the question text (What colour is a lemon: blue or yellow?); 4 stay open (3p-02, 3p-07, 3p-13, 3p-36). The card has no buttons: the options are only in the words.

The reviewers read spoken either/or text as arguably not an answer-choice UI. But MOD-03-U02 (must) says no buttons, choices or score on the card, and DSC-04-04, SRC-01-17 and SRC-01-18 rule out answer choices and a classic quiz. Which reading holds is a judgement on a must, so it is yours.

The cost of either/or: a guessing child is right half the time and the wrong option is often absurd (a spoon for brushing teeth), so 46 of 50 questions are near-trivial. Open questions were dropped because three review rounds kept finding near-miss answers a child could give (a neck warmer for a scarf, a hood for an umbrella).
points: The form of the 3+ questions: either/or in the question text, or open questions.
Whether that form also binds the 4+ and 5+ decks (US-01-03, US-01-04), or each of those stories decides its own.

options.label: Keep either/or for 3+; 4+ and 5+ decide their own form
options.detail: The deck merges as it is (46 either/or, 4 open) and DEC-47 is confirmed for 3+ only, reading MOD-03-U02 as no choice controls on the card. Cost: 46 near-trivial questions; US-01-03 and US-01-04 face the same question again.

options.label: Keep either/or for 3+ and use it for 4+ and 5+ too
options.detail: The deck merges as it is and US-01-03/04 follow the same rule: one form across the app, no repeat of the near-miss problem. Cost: every deck becomes a 50% guess with two options, closer to the classic quiz SRC-01-18 says the app is not.

options.label: Back to open questions for 3+, under a stricter near-miss rule
options.detail: Open questions return, starting from the wording the reviewers accepted; each one with a near miss is reworded to rule it out, and the record names the near miss checked per row. No either/or, a literal fit with MOD-03-U02; 4+/5+ stay open too. Cost: one more content and review round.

options.label: Open by default; either/or only where no rewording removes a near miss
options.detail: Most questions open as in c; the few that cannot be made unambiguous keep two options, each listed with its reason in the record. Fewer rewrites than c, but those cards still carry choices, so MOD-03-U02 is bent for them.

ask.why: It reads MOD-03-U02 and SRC-01-17/18 as written, and it keeps the questions worth asking: a 50% guess against an absurd option teaches little. The near-miss problem is a writing problem the record can control row by row, not a reason to change what a card is.
